This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The petition averments briefly stated as under; That on 18.01.2023 at about 1.30a.m. petitioner had been traveling in mini Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg. No.KA-06-TD-3209-3210 on SH-33 TM Road, near SCCH-5 Kothagere Palya, Kothagere Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur District, at that time,
a Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-B-4015 being driven by its driver from Hebbur side at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the hind portion of tractor. Due to the impact,
petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to CHC,
Kunigal and after first aid he was shifted to AC Giri Hospital, Bellur, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and he had spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses, attendant's charges.

3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 35 years, hale and healthy, working as labourer,
thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. Due to the accident, he became permanently disabled and suffering with deformity.

With regard to accident in crime No.17/2023 is registered SCCH-5 against the driver of the Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-B-4015 before the Kunigal Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has not appeared before court hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.
Further seeks protection under Sec.147 and 149 of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that, driver of the Goods Vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-B-4015 does not possess SCCH-5 valid and effective driving licence and respondent No.2 has issued policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of said vehicle and liability of this respondent is limited to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further denied very occurrence of the alleged accident and also denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner and further submitted that, petition is bad for non-joinder and misjoinder of necessary parties to the p r o c e e d i n g s i . e . , o w n e r a n d i n s u r e r o f T r a c t o r a n d T r a i l o r b e a r i n g R e g . N o .
KA-06-TD-3209/KA-06-TD-3210.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exaggerated, excessive, arbitrary and speculative.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. Based on the pleadings of the parties this court has framed the following:

sentences.text: Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 18.01.2023 at about 1.30 a.m. near Kothagere Palya, Kothagere, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur District due to rash and negligent driving of Goods Vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-B-4015 and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove the case, Petitioner himself examined as PW-1, examined Dr.Ramesh,
Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW-2 and marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence.
SCCH-5 7.
Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record and my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 :

As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove the case, petitioner examined himself as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated.

In order to prove road traffic accident copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar with sketch is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, SCCH-5 copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.7.
9.
Further to substantiate the petitioner's case, petitioner has examined Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1, PW-2 and documents those have marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 corroborates the case of the petitioner about occurrence of the road traffic accident dated 18.01.2023 as alleged in the petition.

10. Per contra, except filing of written statement, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and to discard the evidence of P.W.-1 evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, this Nagaraju vs Krishna G on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104470627/
3 tribunal held that the petitioner sustained the injuries due to the accident occured on 18.01.2023 at about 1.30 a.m. while he was travelling in mini Tractor SCCH-5 and Trailer bearing Reg.
No.KA-06-TD-3209-3210 on SH-33 TM Road, near Kothagere Palya, Kothagere Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur District.
11. It is evident from police papers that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of driver of the Goods Vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-B-4015.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained displaced fracture of middle 1/3rd shaft of ulna right, undisplaced fracture of left patella, for which he took treatment of internal fixation of right ulna and patella fracture treated conservatively.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate SCCH-5 marked as Ex.P.6, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by Adichunchanagiri Hospital & Research Centre, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 18.01.2023 to 31.01.2023.

Further he has exhibited medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.9, medical bills amounting to Rs.12,138/- marked as Ex.P.10.
13.
Further Dr.Ramesh B., Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited OPD Book marked as Ex.P.12 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.13 and he has assessed permanent physical disability of 23% of right upper limb and 8% left lower limb, which is total 11.6% of whole body.
In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner and not seen discharge summary.

Further deposed that,
fractures are united and one side implant are there and with some SCCH-5 difficulty petitioner may do his work by sitting position, treatment of the petitioner is completed, but implants are still pending for removal, muscle power and strength of petitioner is improved.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 10% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body out of 23% of right upper limb and 8% of left lower limb, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

14. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 35 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.11, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 01.01.1987 and the alleged accident is occurred on SCCH-5 18.01.2023, accordingly relying on Ex.P.11 his age is considered about 36 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 15 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s.
Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

To prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.15,250/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.

So petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,608/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
SCCH-5 17.
Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.10 medical bills for Rs.12,138/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is concerned.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.6 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 18.01.2023.

So as per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained CLW of left knee joint, CLW over right forehead, abrasions over right chest in maxillary bone and swelling over right forearm, which are grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Mohan Kumar N.K. and Krishna Murthy for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of SCCH-5 the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
18.
Per contra except denial in the written statement, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to proved the allegations as alleged in the written statement.
In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondent No.2 has filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case.
19. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1.
Loss of Future Income 2,74,500-00 2. Pain and sufferings 15,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges

4. Medical Expenses 12,138-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 SCCH-5 Nagaraju vs Krishna G on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104470627/
5 6. Loss of income during laid up 6,608-00 period Total 3,38,246 -00 Rounded off to Rs.3,38,500/-
20.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,38,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

21. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.PSID368693 which is valid for the period from 29.04.2022 to 28.04.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 18.01.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, respondent No.2/insurer is directed to SCCH-5 deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
within 60 days from the date of this order.hence
this tribunal answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.3,38,500/-
(Rupees Three Lakhs Thirty Eight Thousand Five Hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his SCCH-5 account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
